questions.q: In "Find a gap and a first buyer Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Make a before/after table: cost per unit, waste percent, repeat buyers.
Daily log: date, batch code, cost, units made, sold, waste, complaints.
Never print health claims such as 'cures' or 'boosts immunity'.
Talk to 5 possible buyers (a cafe, a shop, a canteen, neighbours): what do you buy now, how often, what do you pay, what annoys you?

questions.q: In "Food safety as a way of thinking Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Records: a simple daily log of temperatures, cleaning and batch codes is your proof.
Keep a sample of every batch until it expires.
Store and transport at the temperature your tests used.
Write down 10 products with price per kilo or pack (with currency) and who buys them.

questions.q: In "Recipe, scaling and yield Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Safe temperatures: keep cold food cold and hot food hot; the danger zone is the range where germs grow quickly. Use your authority's exact figures.
Scale by a factor, then test: some things (salt, spice, baking time) do not scale in a straight line.
Write a one-page idea: product, buyer, hoped-for price, pack size.
Ask the local food authority to check your label draft before printing.

questions.q: In "Shelf life and storage Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Daily log: date, batch code, cost, units made, sold, waste, complaints.
Records: a simple daily log of temperatures, cleaning and batch codes is your proof.
Change one thing per trial; record taste, texture, colour and yield.
Keep samples of each batch in the same pack as sold and check on days 1, 3, 7 and 14.

questions.q: In "Packs and labels Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Pack choice affects shelf life, cost and waste; avoid over-packing.
Keep a sample of every batch until it expires.
Make a before/after table: cost per unit, waste percent, repeat buyers.
Change one thing per trial; record taste, texture, colour and yield.

questions.q: In "Costing and pricing Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Use a date label that is shorter than the tested life, with a safety margin.
Check the break-even: fixed costs divided by margin per unit.
Yield = weight out divided by weight in. Track it for every batch.
Ask the local food authority to check your label draft before printing.

questions.q: In "Run the 30-day pilot Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write down each complaint: what happened and what you changed.
Give two peers written feedback: one thing strong, one thing to fix.
Convert to weight (grams) not cups: weight is repeatable.
Margin = (price minus cost) divided by price.

questions.q: In "Present, decide and plan Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Four kinds of hazard: germs (biological), chemical, foreign bodies (physical) and allergens.
Give two peers written feedback: one thing strong, one thing to fix.
Write down 10 products with price per kilo or pack (with currency) and who buys them.
Margin = (price minus cost) divided by price.
